text.p: Indonesian retail firm Multipolar said on Tuesday that leading businessman Hari Darmawan had bought an additional five percent stake in the firm, taking his holding to 10 percent.

Multipolar said in a statement that Darmawan, the founder of retailer PT Matahari Putra Prima, had purchased his entire stake over the past month for 56 billion rupiah, or for about 2,025 rupiah per share, from controlling shareholder, the Lippo Group.
Multipolar closed 200 rupiah higher at 1,625 rupiah on Tuesday with 8.1 million shares traded.

"The purchases show my commitment to build Multipolar into Indonesia's premier retailing group not only through my commitment of vision and energy but also in financial terms," Darmawan was quoted as saying in the statement.
Darmawan said he had bought the stake in his individual capacity and would consider further increasing his holdings in Multipolar.

"I have completed my initial plan of a 10 percent holding in Multipolar," he said. "I continue to find Multipolar shares very cheap and attractive. Therefore, I look forward to consider purchasing for my own account additional shares from the open market as and when appropriate."
Multipolar said it welcomed Darmawan's holding in the company and was pleased with the possibility that he would increase his stake further.
